svg.title: The complete PIM-SM workflow in four phases and twelve steps, with the message that does the work at each step
svg.desc: Four phases stacked vertically. Phase one, the receiver joins: the receiver sends an IGMP report, the last-hop router creates (*,G) and sends a PIM (*,G) join toward the RP, and the join travels hop by hop building the shared tree. Phase two, source registration: the source starts sending, the first-hop router encapsulates packets in PIM Register unicast messages to the RP, the RP decapsulates and forwards down the shared tree while joining the source tree, then sends Register-Stop once the source tree exists. Phase three, shortest-path switchover: after the first packet the last-hop router sends an (S,G) join toward the source, then an (S,G) rpt-prune to the RP, and traffic follows the shortest path. Phase four, leaving: the receiver sends a leave, the last-hop router sends a group-specific query, and if nobody answers it prunes hop by hop. A bottom band notes that only phase two is unique to any-source multicast, and that SSM has none of it.
svg.text: Twelve steps, four phases, one asymmetry
Receivers build the tree; sources only announce themselves. Everything else follows from that.
PHASE 1 - THE RECEIVER JOINS (SHARED TREE)
1 receiver -> IGMP Report 239.1.1.1
the last hop now knows someone wants the group
2 LHR -> RP PIM (*,G) Join
builds (*,G) state; the RP address comes from the RP mapping
3 hop by hop toward the RP
each router on the way installs (*,G) and one OIL entry
This is the only phase that ever runs when nobody is sending: a receiver can join a silent group and wait.
PHASE 2 - THE SOURCE REGISTERS (UNICAST WRAPPING)
4 source starts sending
the FHR has no state yet: the packet would be dropped at RPF
5 FHR -> RP PIM Register (unicast)
the multicast packet is encapsulated inside a unicast PIM message
6 RP decapsulates, forwards down (*,G),
and sends (S,G) Join toward the source to pull the real tree
7 RP -> FHR Register-Stop
sent once the source tree exists; the encapsulation ends
If step 7 never arrives you get a register storm: the RP is receiving a copy of every packet forever.
PHASE 3 - SHORTEST-PATH SWITCHOVER (DEFAULT BEHAVIOUR)
8 LHR -> source (S,G) Join
triggered by the first packet, not by a timer or a threshold
9 LHR -> RP (S,G) rpt-prune
cuts the shared-tree branch so traffic does not arrive twice
10 traffic now runs source -> LHR -> receiver
shorter path, but one (S,G) per branch on the source side
PHASE 4 - LEAVING (THE ONLY PART THAT IS LAYER 2 AWARE)
11 receiver -> IGMP Leave
the LHR sends a group-specific query and waits for an answer
12 no answer -> PIM Prune hop by hop
routers with no remaining OIL entry drop the state entirely
A silent leave (host disappears without sending) waits for the group timer instead: this is why IGMP timers matter to multicast routing.
